items.name: marin_sibling_ingestion
items.description: Build a turnkey onboard-and-ingest flow, validate it by onboarding Mill Valley and San Anselmo end-to-end, then update docs so any operator can do the same.
items.source: federation testbed — data prerequisite for cross_marin_query_prototype + operator experience validation
items.notes: Done 2026-03-15. Turnkey onboard script (scripts/onboard.py) generates configs + runs Modal ingestion in one command. Mill Valley: 57 meetings, 166 agenda items, 2 decisions, 591 vectors. San Anselmo: 152 meetings, 34 new agenda items, 112 decisions, 1037 vectors. Both jurisdictions now have non-zero decisions + vectors. Chunks were 0/14 due to Granicus HTML agendas (MV) and SSL cert errors (SA) — not blocking.

items.name: turnkey_onboard_hardening
items.description: Add a validation gate (small sample + quality check before full backfill) and fix data quality gaps: HTML agenda chunk extraction for Granicus, duplicate meeting deduplication, post-onboard quality report, and idempotent re-runs.
items.source: marin_sibling_ingestion validation — gaps found during Mill Valley + San Anselmo onboarding
items.notes: Eight gaps identified: (0) No validation gate — ingests 365 days blind, should sample 30 days first, verify quality (chunks>0? decisions>0?), then scale up only if quality passes. Prevents burning $3-4 on jurisdictions with unextractable data. (1) Chunks=0 for Granicus HTML AgendaViewer sites — need to extract text from GeneratedAgendaViewer HTML pages when no PDF link exists. (2) Only 2/57 decisions for Mill Valley — thin HTML minutes, need quality signal. (3) Duplicate meetings from multi-view archives — view 2 and 3 contain same meetings, wastes LLM spend. (4) No post-onboard quality report — operator can't tell if results are good or bad. (5) County enrichment is fragile string patching on YAML. (6) No idempotency — re-run doubles LLM spend on agenda/decisions. (7) City name sensitivity — slug derivation is case/prefix sensitive. Must fix before open sourcing and before cross-jurisdiction queries can rely on this data.

items.name: cross_marin_query_prototype

items.notes: Infrastructure done: jurisdiction resolution, tier boosting (self=1.0, sibling=0.8), parallel fan-out, semantic relevance scores (04792c2), noise filter MIN_RELEVANCE=0.45, 130+ tests. Data ready: SR 83 decisions, MV 60, SA 96. Decision IDs migrated to meeting-scoped ordinals (f08025f). Remaining: (1) downward resolution — query county-marin should fan out to child cities, (2) cache registry.json in memory, (3) mount v2 on REST API server.

items.name: local_impact_relevance
items.description: Score federal rules by local relevance. Agency-to-topic mapping, geographic text matching, CFR part matching. Extension sorts by relevance, draft_federal_comment shows local context.
items.notes: COMPLETE. Created relevance.py with 3 heuristic signals: (1) agency-to-topic mapping (24 agencies → 13 local policy areas), (2) geographic text matching (San Rafael/Marin/Bay Area/California with tiered weighting), (3) CFR title matching (14 locally relevant CFR titles). Added local_relevance_score FLOAT + relevance_reasons JSONB columns to federal_rules table. Backfilled 4,115 rules: 1,013 scored > 0 (25%). Scores auto-computed on ingest via store_federal_rules(). V2 search sorts federal comment periods by relevance. MCP tools display relevance score + reasons. Chunker includes relevance context in vector text for semantic search.

items.name: vector_llm_relevance_pipeline
items.description: Vector-first relevance pipeline: embed local policy descriptions as query vectors, retrieve candidate federal rules by similarity, LLM-confirm relevance on candidates only. Replaces heuristic-only scoring with semantic + LLM hybrid.
items.source: multi-scale participation — federal data (refinement of local_impact_relevance)
items.notes: 3-stage pipeline: (1) Define 10-15 policy area query vectors for San Rafael (can bootstrap from existing municipal_code embeddings — tested and works, 0.69 similarity for housing, 0.68 for water). (2) For each policy vector, retrieve top 30-50 most similar federal rules via pgvector cosine similarity, deduplicate across policy areas (~200-400 candidates from 4,115 total). (3) Send candidates to gpt-4o-mini in batches of 20-30 for confirmation + local_relevance_summary generation. Store score + summary. Cost: ~$0.05 for full corpus, pennies/week for new rules. Follows existing classify_topics.py batch pattern. Ongoing: new rules auto-scored on ingest after embedding. 1-2 sessions.

Extension CA tab has voice/coordination support but not state-specific content rendering (acceptable for MVP).

items.name: vertical_query_tier_tuning
items.description: Tune tier weights for upward queries (city→state→federal). Parent tier is currently 1.0 (same as self), which means state/federal results compete equally with local decisions. May need level-aware weighting or separate result grouping.
items.notes: With real state/federal data, include_parents=True will return results from 3+ levels. Questions: (1) Should parent weight stay 1.0 or decrease with distance (county=0.9, state=0.7, federal=0.5)? (2) Should jurisdiction_results group by level (local/state/federal) not just jurisdiction ID? (3) How does the extension render mixed-level results? Needs real data to validate — run after federal_comment_periods. 1 session.

items.name: downward_query_scaling
items.description: Cap or paginate downward resolution for state/county-level queries. Querying state-california with include_siblings (downward) would fan out to every CA city — works with 4, breaks with hundreds.
items.notes: Options: (1) cap fan-out at N jurisdictions (e.g., 10), (2) require explicit also_include for large fan-outs, (3) aggregate mode returns counts per jurisdiction without full search. Not urgent until CA has more than ~10 cities. 1 session.

items.name: upcoming_comment_periods
items.description: Implement UpcomingType.comment_periods and UpcomingType.hearings in civic.upcoming. Surface federal comment deadlines and state hearing dates alongside local meetings.
items.notes: UpcomingType enum already has comment_periods and hearings but execute_upcoming() only handles meetings. Need adapters that query stored comment periods/hearings with deadlines. Key UX: show 'Comment period closes in 3 days' alongside 'City Council meets Tuesday'. 1 session, depends on federal_comment_periods data.

items.name: civic_act_federal_comment
items.description: civic.act handlers for federal comment drafting and submission preparation. draft_federal_comment returns structured draft guidance with rule context; prepare_federal_comment returns submission URL, deadline, and instructions. Programmatic submission not supported by regulations.gov — users submit via web form.
items.notes: regulations.gov does not support programmatic POST comment submission (ToS restriction). Implemented draft_federal_comment (AI-assisted draft with stance-aware guidance, rule context, deadline urgency) and prepare_federal_comment (structured submission context for extension UI). Both wired into civic.act via _ACTION_TO_HANDLER, registered as MCP tools in FEDERAL_TOOLS, and ref-parseable from rule:us-federal:{doc_number}.

items.name: legislation_adapter_unification
items.description: Unify legislation data path: query stored state/federal legislation first, fall back to what_applies() API calls. Currently all legislation comes via on-demand API calls regardless of what's stored.
items.notes: LegislationAdapter currently calls what_applies() which hits LegiScan/Federal Register APIs on every query. With stored state/federal data, should check storage first for faster responses and offline capability. API calls become the refresh mechanism, not the query path. 1 session.

items.name: turnkey_state_onboarding
items.description: Generalize state-level onboarding beyond hardcoded CA. Framework for adding other states (legislation source detection, bulk download client generation, server deployment).
items.notes: CA is hardcoded to leginfo.legislature.ca.gov. Other states have different legislation platforms. Deprioritized per roadmap — CA is the only state needed pre-launch. Post-launch work.
